newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Centertel boosts revenue, net profit in '96.
newsitem.headline: Polish Centertel boosts revenue, net profit in '96.

text.p: Polish cellular telephone firm PTK Centertel, in which France Telecom has a 34-percent stake, increased its revenues by 39 percent to 585 million zlotys last year and boosted net profit, the firm said on Wednesday.
"In 1996, we reached revenues of 585 million zlotys, a 39 percent increase compared with 1995," Centertel's director-general Marek Jozefiak told a news conference.
The firm's financial director, Grzegorz Mozdyniewicz, also present, said Centertel substantially increased its net profit last year. He gave no details.
Mozdyniewicz added that Centertel, in which state-owned telecoms monopolist TPSA has a 66-percent stake, planned to invest about $40 million in 1997.
Jozefiak confirmed that Centertel, which uses a dated analogue system for transmission, would bid in a coming tender to build a mobile phone network using a more modern DCS 1800 digital system.
Centertel, which launched operations in Poland in 1991, still leads the market with more than 185,000 customers but its competitors, Era GSM and GSM Plus, are catching up.
Era and Plus, which started operations last year, use digital GSM systems after beating Centertel in a tender for operating licences.
